It's MOSTLY a myth. There have been recorded instances of isolated families that are quite inbred. For instance, the Leeds of New Jersey (from which the Jersey Devil story arose). Basically, it isn't towns, but families. The more isolated you get, the higher likelihood of finding such a family, like the Appalachian mountains.

A much more common phenomenon is widely spread "power families". Say a town has been around since the 1700s, and one family has been there the whole time. Well, that family will have grown quite a bit! And then they'll have married into other families, and spread out, and then returned. So you'll have dozens and dozens of people, all related, all spread throughout a town. After several generations, you do see some light inbreeding. For instance, 2nd or 3rd cousins getting married. Genetically irrelevant at that point, and they're as likely to be respected members of the community as they are to be backwater hicks.
